summary: To provide for the reservation of vacancies in services and posts for members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in West Bengal. The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Vacancies in Services and Posts) Act, 1976 – West Bengal Act XXVII of 1976
text:
Title:
The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Reservation of Vacancies in Services and Posts) Act, 1976 – West Bengal Act XXVII of 1976

Purpose:
To provide for the reservation of vacancies in services and posts for members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in West Bengal.

Key sections:
s3_exclusions: Act does not apply to: Central Government employment, WB Higher Judicial Service, private sector, domestic service, single post cadre.
s4_direct_recruitment: 22% reserved for SC and 6% for ST in direct recruitment. State Govt may increase up to 25% (SC) and 10% (ST). SC/ST candidates qualifying on merit for unreserved posts are not deducted from their quota.
s5_promotion: 22% for SC and 6% for ST in promotion vacancies. No reservation in posts above certain pay scale (Rs 8,700). Separate 50-point roster maintained.
s5A_certificate: SC/ST candidates must support candidature with a certificate of identification under the WB SC&ST (Identification) Act, 1994.
s6_dereservation: No de-reservation by appointing authority. Unfilled reserved vacancies remain unfilled. State Govt may de-reserve in public interest with carry-forward obligation.
s6A_commissioner: Commissioner for Reservation (not below rank of Secretary) ensures reservation compliance for authorities with statewide or Kolkata-based jurisdiction.
s6B_district_commissioner: District Commissioner for Reservation (District Magistrate) ensures compliance for district-level appointing authorities.
s7_penalty: Appointing authority making appointment in contravention: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine of Rs 2,500 or both.
s12_records: Every appointing authority must maintain records and submit annual reports. SC/ST employees adversely affected by non-compliance may notify State Govt.
schedule_I: 100-point roster for direct recruitment. SC vacancies at points: 1,7,11,15,18,21,28,32,36,40,47,51,57,61,65,68,71,78,82,86,90,97. ST vacancies at points: 4,24,43,54,74,93.
schedule_II: 50-point roster for promotion. SC vacancies at points: 1,7,11,15,18,21,28,32,36,40,47. ST vacancies at points: 4,24,43.

Amendments:
WB Act XLII of 1980 – age concession
WB Act XLII of 1984 – percentage change
WB Act XXXI of 1983 – carry forward for promotion
WB Act XLII of 1994 – roster expanded to 100-point; de-reservation procedure revised
WB Act XV of 1996 – District Commissioner for Reservation; school vacancy provisions
WB Act XXIV of 2000 – 100-point roster substituted; commissioner hierarchy expanded; fee waiver; records maintenance
WB Act XXI of 2005 – single post cadre exclusion; cadre definition
WB Act V of 2007 – carry forward clarified; burden of proof on appointing authority
WB Act XIV of 2009 – no reservation above Rs 8,700 pay scale

summary: To provide for the identification of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in West Bengal by certificate. The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994 – West Bengal Act XXXVIII of 1994
text:
Title:
The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994 – West Bengal Act XXXVIII of 1994

Purpose:
To provide for the identification of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in West Bengal by certificate.

Key sections:
s3_sc_identification: Any person belonging to castes/races/tribes specified in Part XIII of the SC Order and resident in the specified locality may be identified by certificate as a member of the Scheduled Castes.
s4_st_identification: Any person belonging to tribes/tribal communities specified in Part XII of the ST Order and resident in the specified locality may be identified by certificate as a member of the Scheduled Tribes.
s5_issuing_authority: Certificates issued by: (a) Sub-Divisional Officer in a district; (b) District Magistrate South 24-Parganas or authorised ADM for Calcutta.
s6_procedure: Certificate issued on application in prescribed form, manner and upon production of prescribed evidence.
s7_refusal: Issuing authority may refuse in writing after giving the person a reasonable opportunity of being heard if not satisfied with evidence.
s8_appeal: Appeal against refusal: (a) to District Magistrate if refused by SDO; (b) to Commissioner Presidency Division if refused by DM/ADM South 24 Parganas. Appeal to be disposed of within 3 months. Decision is final.
s8A_scrutiny_committee: State Scrutiny Committee: Chairperson – Secretary BCW Dept; Convenor – Commissioner BCW Directorate; Expert Member – Director Cultural Research Institute. Powers: verify social status, direct Vigilance Cell, inquire contraventions, cancel/revoke certificates on direction.
s8B_vigilance_cell: District Vigilance Cell: Officer-in-charge not below rank of Dy. SP, up to 3 Inspector-rank investigating officers. Powers: inquire social status claims, investigate contraventions, call for information and documents.
s9_cancellation: Issuing authority may cancel/impound/revoke certificate obtained by false information, misrepresentation, suppression, or forgery. Scrutiny Committee may direct cancellation.
s10_penalty: Obtaining certificate by false information, misrepresentation, suppression or forgery: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to Rs 5,000 or both. (Amended from 6 months/Rs 2,000 by WB Act IV of 2007.)
s11_validation: Certificates issued by competent authority prior to commencement of this Act remain valid unless proved to have been obtained fraudulently.
s11A_verification_by_employer: If appointing authority doubts authenticity of a certificate, it shall send the certificate to the Scrutiny Committee for verification.
s12_rules: State Government may make rules for carrying out purposes of this Act.

Amendments:
WB Act IV of 2007 – inserted s2(a) definition of 'Committee'; inserted s8A (State Scrutiny Committee); inserted s8B (Vigilance Cell); renumbered s9 as s9(1) and inserted s9(2); increased penalty in s10; inserted s11A (verification by employer)

Title:
No. 6316-BCW/MR-84/10 – Kolkata Gazette Extraordinary, 24 September 2010

Purpose:
In exercise of powers under sections 10 and 11 of the WB SC&ST (Reservation of Vacancies in Services and Posts) Act 1976, supersedes all previous orders and notifies the Model 100-Point Roster for direct recruitment along with OBC reserved positions.

Model 100-Point Roster: 1st SC, 2nd UR, 3rd UR, 4th ST, 5th UR, 6th UR, 7th SC, 8th UR, 9th UR, 10th UR, 11th SC, 12th UR, 13th UR, 14th UR, 15th SC, 16th UR, 17th UR, 18th SC, 19th UR, 20th UR, 21st SC, 22nd UR, 23rd UR, 24th ST, 25th UR, 26th UR, 27th UR, 28th SC, 29th UR, 30th UR, 31st UR, 32nd SC, 33rd UR, 34th UR, 35th UR, 36th SC, 37th UR, 38th UR, 39th UR, 40th SC, 41st UR, 42nd UR, 43rd ST, 44th UR, 45th UR, 46th UR, 47th SC, 48th UR, 49th UR, 50th UR, 51st SC, 52nd UR, 53rd UR, 54th ST, 55th UR, 56th UR, 57th SC, 58th UR, 59th UR, 60th UR, 61st SC, 62nd UR, 63rd UR, 64th UR, 65th SC, 66th UR, 67th UR, 68th SC, 69th UR, 70th UR, 71st SC, 72nd UR, 73rd UR, 74th ST, 75th UR, 76th UR, 77th UR, 78th SC, 79th UR, 80th UR, 81st UR, 82nd SC, 83rd UR, 84th UR, 85th UR, 86th SC, 87th UR, 88th UR, 89th UR, 90th SC, 91st UR, 92nd UR, 93rd ST, 94th UR, 95th UR, 96th UR, 97th SC, 98th UR, 99th UR, 100th UR.

In the model roster those shown as 'Unreserved': 9th, 19th, 29th, 49th, 59th, 69th and 89th vacancies shall be reserved for backward classes under Category-B and 6th, 13th, 26th, 38th, 45th, 52nd, 63rd, 76th, 84th and 99th vacancies shall be reserved for backward classes under Category-A of backward classes of citizens included in the lists as defined in clause (c) of section 2 of the West Bengal Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993.

Key provisions:
Supersedes all previous roster orders
Establishes the definitive Model 100-Point Roster for direct recruitment
SC reserved positions (22 out of 100): 1,7,11,15,18,21,28,32,36,40,47,51,57,61,65,68,71,78,82,86,90,97
ST reserved positions (6 out of 100): 4,24,43,54,74,93
OBC Category-B positions (7 out of 100): 9,19,29,49,59,69,89
OBC Category-A positions (10 out of 100): 6,13,26,38,45,52,63,76,84,99
Total reserved = 22+6+7+10 = 45 out of 100 positions

Title:
No. 2976-BCW/MR-167/14 dated 11.09.2014

Purpose:
Clarifies the procedure for issuing OBC caste certificates to adopted children of OBC parents, drawing an analogy from the SC/ST adoption procedure.

Text:
With reference to above this to intimate that the Government of India's Memo No. 35/1/72-R.U. (SCT.V) dated 2nd May, 1975 incorporating (in Para-5) the procedure of issuing Caste Certificates to the adopted sons and daughters of different persons belonging to SC/ST category can be applied mutatis mutandis in case of granting of OBC Certificates to the adopted sons and daughters of the parents belonging to OBC category.

In fact the Memo No. 374-TW-EC dated 27th July, 1994 is somewhat explicit in this matter.

The cases of granting Caste Certificate to the adopted children of OBC parents may be dealt with accordingly.

summary: Procedure for issuance of amended OBC certificates following introduction of Category A & B classification Key provisions: Triggered by Order No. 2770-BCW/MR-116/12 dated 29.08.2014 introducing Category A & B classification for 24 OBC communities; Holders of old OBC certificates must apply for an amended certificate with original certificate and non-creamy layer proof; Certificate issuing authority must re-verify non-creamy layer status and assign Category A or B
text:
Subject:
Procedure for issuance of amended OBC certificates following introduction of Category A & B classification

Text:
Since the status of a person belonging to 'Creamy Layer' changes with time and consequent upon modification of nomenclature of twenty four (24) enlisted Other Backward Classes (OBCs) of this State, vide Order No. 2770-BCW/MR-116/12, dt. 29.08.2014, and introduction of categorization of OBC persons into Category A & Category B as per their relative backwardness there is a need of issuance of amended OBC certificates from the concerned certificate issuing authority in order to avail the benefits of reservation.

In view of this and after careful consideration of all aspects, it has been decided that such amended OBC certificates will be issued in the following manner:-

a) The OBC certificate holder is required to apply for the amended certificate in plain paper to the concerned certificate issuing authority along with original OBC certificate and attested documentary proof in support of non-creamy layer status along with two copies of recent passport sized coloured photograph.

b) Certificate Issuing authority, after categorizing the applicant into Category-A or Category-B as per his/her relative backwardness and being fully satisfied of the applicant's non 'Creamy Layer' status (fresh field enquiry, if needed, is suggested), shall issue a fresh OBC certificate with new Certificate number and date against old certificate number.

Aforesaid procedure is applicable in respect of certificates either issued on-line or are issued manually and data of which are available in the Central Server.

c) In case of the OBC certificates, which were issued manually but there are no data in the central server the age-old method of stamping will continue provided the certificate issuing authority is satisfied about the non-creamy layer status of the applicant.

d) During this process if it is seen that the applicant belongs to the 'Creamy Layer' then obviously the new certificate will not be issued to the incumbent. The enquiry report establishing him/her belonging to 'Creamy Layer' along with the old certificate should be preserved properly to handle any subsequent legal eventuality.

The same procedure may be used for issuance of duplicate OBC certificate, subject to usual checks.

Key provisions:
Triggered by Order No. 2770-BCW/MR-116/12 dated 29.08.2014 introducing Category A & B classification for 24 OBC communities
Holders of old OBC certificates must apply for an amended certificate with original certificate and non-creamy layer proof
Certificate issuing authority must re-verify non-creamy layer status and assign Category A or B
Fresh certificate issued with new number against old certificate number
Certificates in central server (online or manually entered) follow new procedure; certificates not in central server continue with stamping method
If applicant found to be Creamy Layer, new certificate is denied and enquiry report preserved
Same procedure applies for duplicate OBC certificates

summary: Updated Guidelines for Issuance of OBC Certificates (superseding Memo No. 1464-BCW/MR-59/10 dated 30.04.2010) Key provisions: Comprehensive updated guidelines superseding Memo No. 1464-BCW/MR-59/10 dated 30.04.2010; OBC entitlement: member of notified community + non-creamy layer (income below Rs. 6 lakh); Online application at www.castcertificatewb.gov.in; physical documents on 2nd and 4th Wednesdays within 60 days
text:
Subject:
Updated Guidelines for Issuance of OBC Certificates (superseding Memo No. 1464-BCW/MR-59/10 dated 30.04.2010)

Text:
Guidelines for issuance of Other Backward Classes Certificates were issued vide Memo No. 1464-BCW/MR-59/10 dated 30.04.2010. Since then there have been a number of modifications / changes in the orders and notifications necessitating modification of such guidelines.

Therefore, in supersession of the previous guidelines issued in this respect and in compilation and amplification of the provisions already altered the Governor is pleased to issue the following guidelines for receipt and disposal of applications for issuance of OBC Certificates.

1. Provision for Identification: There is no Act regulating identification of persons belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBC). The relevant procedures and provisions applicable for identification of SC & ST as entailed in The SC&ST (Identification) Act 1994 and rules framed there under will be applicable for identification of OBC persons mutatis mutandis with appropriate modifications.

2. Nomenclature: Caste Identification Certificate issued to OBC person is popularly called as Caste Certificate. A format of Caste Certificate to be issued to OBC person is appended to these guidelines. The certificate format is enclosed.

3. Certificate Issuing Authority: As per Notification no-374 (71) –TW/EC/MR-103/94 dated 27/7/1994, the Sub Divisional Officer of a Sub-Division in a District is certificate issuing authority. In Kolkata such certificate is issued by such an officer as the State Government by modification authorizes. Accordingly, the District Welfare Officer, Kolkata and Ex-officio Joint Director, BCW has been notified to act as the certificate issuing authority in respect of Kolkata covering the jurisdiction of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation.

4. Recommending Authority: In a Block area, Block Development Officer is the Recommending Authority in respect of issuance of certificate. In Municipal areas, a Deputy Magistrate under a Sub-Division acts as Recommending Authority. In Kolkata, Backward Classes Welfare Officer, Kolkata acts as Recommending Authority. Backward Classes Inspectors or any other Officer of the same rank acts as enquiring officer in respect of issuance of caste certificate.

5. Entitlement:
a. Any person belonging to any of the category of communities as entailed in orders in the State of West Bengal may be identified to be a member of the OBC provided the incumbent does not belong to the 'creamy layer' i.e. his family income does not exceed the prescribed limit of Rs 6 Lakh subject to provision from time to time.
b. There is no age restriction for being eligible to apply for caste certificate. So no age proof for this purpose is necessary.

6. Application: Application for issuance of Caste Certificate can be filed online in the website address at www.castcertificatewb.gov.in. When an application is made online, the applicant gets an acknowledgement with a receipt number and with information as to the steps to be taken by him to obtain the certificate. After filing the application, the applicant will have to download a copy of the filled in application along with the acknowledgement and then submit the filled in application duly signed along with the documents, if any, in support of his claim on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays of a month within 60 days from the date of filing of his online application. The applicant will have to upload his current passport size photograph at the time of filing the application. On the date of his appearance at the concerned Block/Sub-Division Office he will have to bring originals as well as copies of his documents for verification by the officials. Self attested copies of all the documents, excepting attested copies proving his non-creamy layer status for each application as required will be accepted subject to verification with the originals. In addition to these documents, proof of residing in West Bengal prior to the cut-off date (15/03/93) is also required.

7. Intimation under Right to Public Services Act: As issuance of Caste Certificate has been brought under the purview of the West Bengal Right to Public Services Act, 2013, (WBRTPSA 2013) a receipt in Form 1 will also be given to the applicant on submission of the physical copy of the application along with all the documents.

8. Requirements for obtaining a Caste Certificate: In order to obtain a Caste Certificate for OBC an applicant has to fulfill the following criteria:
a) The applicant must be a citizen of India.
b) He has to be a permanent resident of West Bengal since 15/3/1993.
c) He is an ordinary resident at the address currently residing.
d) He belongs to the said category he/she claims to belong to.
e) His identity.
f) That the applicant does not fall under 'creamy layer'.

9. Eligibility Criteria (Criteria in details):
a) For Citizenship: Citizenship of an applicant may be ascertained from any of the following documents:
   i) Citizenship Certificate
   ii) Voter Identity Card of self or parent(s) (EPIC)
   iii) Authenticated Voter List of self or parent(s)
   iv) Permanent Account Number (PAN) Card of self or parent(s)
   v) Birth Certificate from Competent Authority
   vi) Caste Certificate of father/ Caste Certificates of persons having direct blood relations with the applicant from paternal side
   vii) Any Govt. Document proving citizenship

b) Permanent residence: Permanent residence of an applicant may be ascertained from any of the following documents:
   i) Land deed or land tax receipt
   ii) Voter List proving residence since 15/03/1993
   iii) Birth Certificate proving residence since 15/03/1993
   iv) Ration Card proving residence since 15/03/1993
   v) Caste Certificate of parent(s)
   vi) Any Govt. Document proving permanent residence since 15/03/1993.

c) For local residence: One of the following documents may be accepted:
   i) Land deed or land tax receipt
   ii) Voter Identity Card of self or parent(s)
   iii) Certificate from Competent Authority
   iv) Caste Certificate of parent(s)
   v) Birth Certificate
   vi) Ration Card
   vii) Rent receipt
   viii) Pass Book of a Nationalized Bank, Gramin Bank, Post office or Co-operative Bank
   ix) BPL Card
   x) Any Govt. Document proving local residence.

d) Caste identity: One of the following documents may be accepted:
   i) Caste certificate of any relatives having blood relation with the applicant from paternal side and proof of such relation (genealogical tree/chart)
   ii) Copy of old land deed (prior to 1950) specifying community name in that document
   iii) Any Govt. Document proving Caste identity.

e) For identity: One of the following documents may be accepted:
   i) Admit Card
   ii) EPIC of the applicant.
   iii) PAN Card
   iv) Birth Certificate from Competent Authority
   v) Identity Card by Employer/Educational Institution
   vi) Pass Book of Bank Account
   vii) BPL Card.
   viii) Any Govt. Document proving identity

10. Procedure for disposal:
A. An application filed online is received in Block offices in respect of the applicants living in Block areas and in Sub-Division offices for applicants living in Municipal areas within the Sub-Division. In case of Kolkata, such applications are received at the office of the District Welfare Officer, Kolkata. On the appointed date i.e. on 2nd and 4th Wednesdays of a month and within 60 days from the date of filing the application, the applicant has to appear with physical copy of the application and documents for verification.

B. Procedure for disposal of application when no documentary evidence is available: It is apparent that most of the applicants for OBC certificates are unable to produce such certificate of paternal blood relation as a proof of class identity. In those cases, their class identity is to be decided on field enquiry and public hearing. In those cases, to facilitate easy identification, in deserving cases, an affidavit from the applicant in the format attached to this order, may be obtained wherein the applicant is to declare his eligibility to obtain OBC certificate.

C. Declarations by five to ten local persons certifying the applicant's class identity are NOT required for disposal of OBC certificate application. Field enquiry and/or public hearing may be held where documentary proof is not available.

D. When an application is accompanied by a caste certificate issued to a relative of the applicant from paternal side having blood relation with the applicant and the relationship as well the veracity of the certificate thus submitted is established, the application for caste certificate can be accepted without further enquiry subject to the applicants' belonging to non-creamy layer.

E. Regarding determination of 'Creamy Layer':
   i. Status of the parents (not of the applicant) is to be ascertained. If any of the parents holds a constitutional post or belong to Class I or Group 'A' service of the Central or State Government before the age of 40, he is considered to belong to 'creamy layer'. If both parents belong to class II or Group 'B' service the Central or State Government before the age of 40, he is considered to belong to 'creamy layer'. If such parents retire or die after retirement, the status will remain unchanged.
   ii. Criteria for creamy layer apply mutatis mutandis to sons and daughters of persons holding equivalent posts in PSUs, Banks, Insurance Organisations, Universities, Educational Institutions and comparable private employment.
   iii. When creamy layer status is determined on service/post held by parents, their salary income is not considered. Employees in Government Departments, PSUs, Banks, Insurance Organisations, Educational Institutions will not fall under 'Creamy Layer' unless income from other sources alone (without salary or agricultural land) exceeds Rs. 6 lakh.
   iv. Per Income/Wealth Test: income from salaries and from other sources [other than salaries and agricultural land] is determined separately. If either exceeds Rs. 6.0 lakh per annum or the parent possesses wealth above the Wealth Tax exemption limit for three consecutive years, the sons and daughters fall in creamy layer. Agricultural land income is not considered.

F. An application for caste certificate shall ordinarily be disposed of within four weeks from the date of receipt of the application (Subject to Rule 4, 5, of RTPS Rule 2013).

G. The certificate issuing authority needs to keep in mind that the caste certificate is either issued or denied on the basis of Sec 7 of the West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994.

H. Proper record of the information/evidence collected has to be kept and specific recommendation either in favour or against the applicant has to be forwarded to the Superior Authority.

11. Caste Certificate to migrants:
a. When a person migrates from one State to another after the dates of notification introducing reservation for Other Backward Classes (15/03/1993), he can claim to belong to Other Backward Classes only in relation to the State he originally belonged and not in respect of the State to which he has migrated.
b. Issuance of caste certificate to the migrants is not covered under the on-line system.

12. Scrutiny Committee and District Vigilance Cell: State Scrutiny Committee set up by the State Government with the Secretary, BCW Department as the Chairperson shall deal with matters relating to issuance of OBC certificates also.

13. Cancellation, impounding or revocation of caste certificate: The provisions and procedures as applicable for similar actions for SC&ST Certificates are applicable here mutatis mutandis.

14. Renewal of Caste Certificate of OBC: Since issuance of OBC certificate is dependent on the 'Creamy layer' status which is supposed to change in every year so the certificate holder may approach for revalidation/renewal of the certificate.

15. Appellate Authority: District Magistrate of the concerned district is the Appellate Authority in respect of certificates issued by a Sub-Divisional Officer of that district. In Kolkata, Divisional Commissioner, Presidency Division is the Appellate Authority.

16. Affidavit, Genealogical chart verification, and Cases of adoption: Similar provisions for SC/ST apply mutatis mutandis.

Key provisions:
Comprehensive updated guidelines superseding Memo No. 1464-BCW/MR-59/10 dated 30.04.2010
OBC entitlement: member of notified community + non-creamy layer (income below Rs. 6 lakh)
Online application at www.castcertificatewb.gov.in; physical documents on 2nd and 4th Wednesdays within 60 days
Covered under WB Right to Public Services Act 2013 – Form 1 receipt mandatory
No age restriction for applying; no age proof required
Six eligibility criteria: citizenship, permanent WB residence since 15/03/1993, local residence, caste identity, identity, non-creamy layer
Aadhaar not yet in list (added later by Memo 921-BCW, 2017)
Detailed Creamy Layer determination rules – parental service/income test
Migrants from other States can get certificate but not entitled to WB reservation benefits
Disposal timeline: four weeks from date of receipt (RTPS Rules 2013)
Appellate Authority: District Magistrate (outside Kolkata); Divisional Commissioner Presidency Division (Kolkata)
Three annexures appended: certificate format, affidavit by applicant, affidavit by parent

summary: Verification of applicant documents to prevent misrepresentation of name/surname in caste certificate applications Key provisions: Issued in response to detected fraud: applicants misrepresenting or altering names/surnames to gain unfair advantage; Issuing authorities must verify original educational certificates – mark sheets, admit cards, pass certificates; Priority document: certificate of first public examination (Madhyamik or equivalent)
text:
Subject:
Verification of applicant documents to prevent misrepresentation of name/surname in caste certificate applications

Text:
I am directed to state that it has come to the notice of this Department that while applying for caste certificates some candidates are taking unfair means by suppression / misrepresentation of facts or by altering name /surname to their advantage.

In view of the above, I am further directed to intimate that-

a) Applicants' educational qualification and original supporting certificates need to be seen and verified/checked especially that of the mark-sheet, admit card and/or pass certificate, of course in applicable cases.

b) A notice informing the applicants of that requirement is to be put up in the Notice Board of all concerned offices.

c) Emphasis needs to be given to the documents of the first public examination like Madhyamik or equivalent the incumbent appeared.

d) In case the applicants are yet to appear in this kind of examination, the name and surname recorded in the school register shall be followed while issuing caste certificate.

e) The caste certificate mandatorily needs to be issued in the name as recorded in that educational certificate of the first public examination or otherwise as mentioned in Para (d) and guardians' name shall also be same in that certificate or otherwise as mentioned in Para (d), irrespective of the way of applicant has written/entered/typed the names in the application form.

The letter is issued with the concurrence of the competent authority.

Key provisions:
Issued in response to detected fraud: applicants misrepresenting or altering names/surnames to gain unfair advantage
Issuing authorities must verify original educational certificates – mark sheets, admit cards, pass certificates
Priority document: certificate of first public examination (Madhyamik or equivalent)
For applicants yet to appear in public exam: name in school register governs
Caste certificate MUST be issued in the name as per first public exam certificate regardless of how applicant typed name in application form
Guardian's name in certificate must also match educational records
Notice to be displayed on Notice Boards of all concerned offices

summary: Foundational policy document implementing EWS (Economically Weaker Sections) reservation in West Bengal, consequent to the Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019, which inserted Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) into the Constitution of India. Office Memorandum No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019 dated 09.07.2019 – Personnel and Administrative Reforms Department, Administrative Reforms Cell Key provisions: Constitutional basis: Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act 2019 inserting Articles 15(6) and 16(6); State Cabinet adopted policy on 02/07/2019; 10% reservation for EWS in direct recruitment in civil posts/services and admission to educational institutions
text:
Title:
Office Memorandum No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019 dated 09.07.2019 – Personnel and Administrative Reforms Department, Administrative Reforms Cell

Purpose:
Foundational policy document implementing EWS (Economically Weaker Sections) reservation in West Bengal, consequent to the Constitution (One Hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019, which inserted Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) into the Constitution of India.

Text:
In order to enable the Economically Weaker Sections (EWSs) who are not covered under the existing scheme of reservations for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and the Socially and Educationally Backward Classes, to receive the benefits of reservation on a preferential basis in civil posts and services in the Government of West Bengal, the State Cabinet, in commensurate with the Constitution (One hundred and Third Amendment) Act, 2019, has adopted in its meeting on 02/07/2019 a policy on reservation to EWSs in Civil Post and Services in Government of West Bengal as well as for admission in Educational Institutions in West Bengal.

QUANTUM OF RESERVATION: The persons belonging to EWSs who are not covered under the scheme of reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs shall get 10% reservation in direct recruitment in civil posts and services in the Government of West Bengal and for admission in Educational Institutions in West Bengal.

EXEMPTION FROM RESERVATION: Scientific, Technical and certain other posts to be notified by the State Government which satisfy all the following conditions will be exempted: (a) Posts in grades above the lowest grade in Group A; (b) Scientific, Technical and certain other posts for which qualifications in natural sciences, exact sciences, applied sciences or technology or certain prescribed speciality are essential and the incumbents have to use that knowledge in discharge of their duties; (c) Posts for conducting or organising or guiding or directing research.

Reservation for admission will not be applicable to Minority Educational Institutions referred to in Clause (1) of Article 30 of the Constitution of India.

ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: (i) Persons who are not covered under the scheme of reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs; (ii) Gross annual family income should be below Rs. 8.00 lakh (Rupees Eight lakh only). Income shall include income from all sources i.e. salary, agriculture, business, profession, etc. for the financial year prior to the year of application; (iii) Persons whose families do not own or possess any of the following assets: (a) 5 acres agricultural land and above; (b) Residential flat of 1000 sq. ft and above; (c) Residential plot of 100 sq. yards and above in notified municipalities; (d) Residential plot of 200 sq. yards and above in areas other than the notified municipalities. The property held by a family in different locations would be clubbed together for determining EWS status.

FAMILY DEFINITION: The term 'family' for this purpose will include the persons who seek benefits of reservation, his/her parents and siblings below the age of 18 years as also his/her spouse and children below the age of 18 years.

INCOME AND ASSET CERTIFICATE ISSUING AUTHORITY: The benefit of reservation under EWS can be availed upon production of an Income and Asset Certificate issued by any of the following authorities in prescribed format as given in Annexure-C: (1) District Magistrate / Additional District Magistrate; (2) Sub-Divisional Officer; (3) DWO, Kolkata for Kolkata Municipal Corporation area.

APPLICATION PROCEDURE: Persons seeking Income and Asset Certificate shall apply in Annexure-A format to: (1) Block Development Officers for rural areas; (2) Sub-Divisional Officer for Municipalities; (3) DWO, Kolkata for KMC areas.

List of supporting documents (illustrative, not exhaustive): (a) EPIC or Citizenship Certificate of self or parents; (b) PAN Card; (c) Birth Certificate / Admit Card / Certificate of Madhyamik or equivalent; (d) Pay Slip; (e) Income Certificate from prescribed authorities; (f) Residential Certificate; (g) RoR/Parcha/Registered Deed; (h) Certificate from Prodhan of Gram Panchayat / Chairman of Municipality / Councillor; (i) Self Declaration (Annexure-B).

ENQUIRY AND VERIFICATION: On receipt of application the receiving authority shall ask the applicant to appear within two weeks for hearing and submission of proofs before: (1) Inspector BCW for Panchayat and Municipal areas; (2) DWO Kolkata / IBCW for KMC area. Verification of immovable assets by BL & LRO for Panchayat/Municipal areas; BL & LRO / Chief Valuer/Surveyor for KMC areas.

APPOINTMENT CLAUSE: Offer of appointment must include clause that appointment is provisional and subject to Income and Asset Certificate verification; if verification reveals fake/false claim, services terminated forthwith without assigning reasons and IPC action for production of fake/false certificate.

ADJUSTMENT AGAINST UNRESERVED VACANCIES: EWS person cannot be denied the right to compete for unreserved vacancy. Merit-based selections not counted towards EWS reservation quota.

EFFECTIVE RESERVATION – MAINTENANCE OF ROSTERS: BCW Department entrusted with maintenance of post-based reservation roster for other categories of reservation. A single post-based reservation roster for EWS interpolating with SCs, STs and OBCs to be prepared and circulated by BCW Department. If EWS roster point coincides with SC/ST/OBC roster point, next available UR roster point allotted to EWS ('squeezing' principle). Every Government establishment shall recast group-wise post-based reservation roster.

RESERVATION DURING ADMISSION: EWS reservation equally applicable during admission to educational institutions including private aided/unaided institutions (except minority institutions), subject to maximum of 10% of total seats in each category. Departments of Health & Family Welfare, Higher Education and School Education to bring out necessary guidelines.

Key provisions:
Constitutional basis: Constitution (103rd Amendment) Act 2019 inserting Articles 15(6) and 16(6)
State Cabinet adopted policy on 02/07/2019
10% reservation for EWS in direct recruitment in civil posts/services and admission to educational institutions
EWS defined as: not SC/ST/OBC + family income below Rs. 8 lakh + does not own disqualifying assets
Asset disqualification: 5 acres agricultural land, 1000 sq ft residential flat, 100 sq yard plot in municipalities, 200 sq yard plot elsewhere
Family definition: applicant + parents + siblings below 18 + spouse + children below 18
Income and Asset Certificate issued by: DM/ADM, SDO, DWO Kolkata (KMC area)
Application submitted to: BDO (rural), SDO (municipal), DWO Kolkata (KMC)
EWS roster to be interpolated with existing SC/ST/OBC 100-point roster; 'squeezing' principle applies
Appointment provisional until certificate verified; fake certificate leads to dismissal and IPC action
EWS merit candidates not counted against reservation quota
Not applicable to Minority Educational Institutions (Article 30(1))
Annexures: A – Application form; B – Self-Declaration; C – Income and Asset Certificate format (state use)
Copies forwarded to all secretaries/departments of Government of West Bengal

text:
Subject:
Introduction of digitally signed caste certificates through e-signature for all Sub-Divisions of West Bengal

Text:
Whereas the Caste Certificates to SC/ST/OBC Communities under the West Bengal Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994, are presently issued with manual (physical) signature of the issuing authority i.e. by the concerned Sub Divisional Officers in the Districts;

Whereas under Ease of Doing Business and Business Action Reforms Plan of Government of West Bengal mandated for digitization of the issuance of Caste Certificate through e-signature of issuing authority as per provisions of Section 2(1)(p) of IT Act, 2000, it was decided to introduce digitally signed Caste Certificates;

Whereas in terms of Order No. BCW-22099/6/2022-SECTION(BCW)-Dept. of BCW/497349 dated 29.09.2022 digitally signed Caste Certificates were introduced in respect of issuing authorities in Bidhannagar Sub-division under North 24 Parganas District, Sadar Sub-division under South 24 Parganas District, Sadar Sub-Division under Howrah District and the Kolkata District with effect from 29.09.2022;

Now, the Governor is pleased to introduce digitally signed Caste Certificates through e-signature in respect of issuing authorities in rest of the Sub-divisions of West Bengal.

This order will take immediate effect.

Key provisions:
Completes the statewide rollout of digitally signed caste certificates (e-signature) across all Sub-Divisions of West Bengal
Legal basis: Section 2(1)(p) of IT Act, 2000; mandated under WB Ease of Doing Business and Business Action Reforms Plan
Pilot phase (Order dated 29.09.2022) had already covered: Bidhannagar Sub-division (North 24 Parganas), Sadar Sub-division (South 24 Parganas), Sadar Sub-Division (Howrah), and Kolkata District
This notification (21.10.2022) extends e-signature to all remaining Sub-Divisions of West Bengal

summary: Inserts a new Section 9A into the WB SC/ST Identification Act, 1994, providing a right of appeal against cancellation, impounding or revocation of caste certificates, which previously had no statutory appeal mechanism. West Bengal Act XIII of 2022 – The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) (Amendment) Act, 2022 Key provisions: Gap filled: prior to this amendment, Section 9 of the 1994 Act allowed cancellation/impounding/revocation of caste certificates but provided NO statutory right of appeal against such cancellation – this amendment creates that right; New Section 9A inserted after Section 9; Appeal against cancellation/impounding/revocation by SDO → lies to District Magistrate or authorised ADM
text:
Title:
West Bengal Act XIII of 2022 – The West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) (Amendment) Act, 2022

Purpose:
Inserts a new Section 9A into the WB SC/ST Identification Act, 1994, providing a right of appeal against cancellation, impounding or revocation of caste certificates, which previously had no statutory appeal mechanism.

Text:
West Bengal Act XIII of 2022 – THE WEST BENGAL SCHEDULED CASTES AND SCHEDULED TRIBES (IDENTIFICATION) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022.

An Act to amend the West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994.

WHEREAS it is expedient to amend the West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994, for the purpose and in the manner hereinafter appearing;

It is hereby enacted in the Seventy-third year of the Republic of India, by the Legislature of West Bengal, as follows:

1. (1) This Act may be called the West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) (Amendment) Act, 2022.
(2) It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

2. After section 9 of the West Bengal Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Identification) Act, 1994, the following section shall be inserted:

'Appeal against cancellation etc. of certificates.
9A. (1) An appeal against any cancellation, impounding or revocation of the certificate under sub-section (1) of section 9 shall lie—
(a) to the District Magistrate, or the Additional District Magistrate authorised by the District Magistrate in this behalf, where the certificate is cancelled or impounded or revoked by the Sub-Divisional Officer, and
(b) to the Commissioner, Presidency Division, where the certificate is cancelled or impounded or revoked by an officer authorised under clause (b) of section 5, as the case may be:

Provided that every such appeal shall be made in such manner and within such time as may be prescribed:
Provided further that every such appeal shall be disposed of within three months from the date on which that appeal has been made:
Provided also that no such appeal shall be disposed of without giving the appellant a reasonable opportunity of being heard.

(2) The decision of the District Magistrate or the Additional District Magistrate or the Commissioner, Presidency Division, as the case may be, on any appeal under sub-section (1) shall be final.'

Key provisions:
Gap filled: prior to this amendment, Section 9 of the 1994 Act allowed cancellation/impounding/revocation of caste certificates but provided NO statutory right of appeal against such cancellation – this amendment creates that right
New Section 9A inserted after Section 9
Appeal against cancellation/impounding/revocation by SDO → lies to District Magistrate or authorised ADM
Appeal against cancellation/impounding/revocation by officer under Section 5(b) (DM South 24 Parganas / ADM for Calcutta) → lies to Commissioner, Presidency Division
Time limit for disposal of appeal: 3 months from the date of appeal
Natural justice: no appeal to be disposed of without giving the appellant a reasonable opportunity of being heard
Decision of DM/ADM/Commissioner Presidency Division on appeal is FINAL
Commencement: to be notified separately – not self-executing
Mirrors the structure of the existing Section 8 (appeal against refusal to issue certificate), now symmetrically extended to cancellations

text:
Title:
Memorandum No. 959-BCW/MR-52/2019 dated 18.05.2023

Purpose:
BCW Department (acting as Nodal Department for EWS reservation) issues modifications to the EWS certificate issuance procedure and strengthens the reservation system for EWS, building on the foundational P&AR Memo 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019 dated 09.07.2019.

Text:
In continuation of the Office Memorandum No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019 dated 9th July, 2019, issued by the Personnel & Administrative Reforms Department (Administrative Reforms Cell), Government of West Bengal, to provide benefits of reservation in civil posts and services in the Government of West Bengal and also in admission to educational institutions in West Bengal for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWSs), the following modifications are issued in the capacity of Nodal Department for EWS reservation, for receipt and disposal of applications for issuance of EWS certificate and strengthening reservation system for the EWS.

1. Nomenclature: Economically Weaker Sections (EWSs) is a term that describes the persons who are not covered under the scheme of reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes with income and assets below the criteria as set by the government. EWS certificate is the proof that a person belongs to the EWS category and is eligible to avail the reservation benefits meant for the EWS.

2. Quantum of Reservation: The persons belonging to EWS shall get 10% reservation in direct recruitment in civil posts and services in all its departments/ boards/ corporations/local bodies in the Government of West Bengal and also in admission to Educational Institutions in the state of West Bengal.

3. Eligibility Criteria for reservation under EWS: As stated in the Office Memorandum No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019 dated 09.07.2019.

4. Issuance of EWS Certificate:
I. Issuing Authority: (A) Additional District Magistrate in charge of development matters of the District concerned; (B) District Welfare Officer, Kolkata and Ex-officio Joint Director, BCW & TD in respect of Kolkata covering the jurisdiction of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation.
II. Enquiry, verifying and recommending authority: Appropriate authorities shall be determined by the issuing authority.

5. Mode of submission of Application: Application for issuance of EWS Certificate has to be filed online (to be notified later) through the Government portal. Application will be submitted in offline mode at present until the introduction of online system within 3 months. Additional documents required with Annexure-A: (a) Aadhaar Card/Khadyasathi card of applicant; (b) PAN Card of applicant and other family members (whichever applicable).

6. List of supporting documents (Illustrative and not exhaustive): In addition to documents in OM No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019, Aadhaar Card/Khadyasathi card and PAN Card required.

7. Validity of EWS certificate: EWS certificate is valid for the financial year of issuance of certificate.

8. EWS certificate to those persons who have shifted from other states and residing in the state of West Bengal: Person who has shifted from other state, has to be a resident of State of West Bengal to avail reservation under EWS category as per applicable norms of Government of West Bengal.

9. Issuance of EWS certificate for those OBCs who are included in the State list but not in the Central list: If a person belongs to OBC category (A & B) in the State OBC list of West Bengal but not in the Central OBC list for this state, he/she can apply for EWS certificate for recruitment in civil posts/services and admission in educational institutions under Govt. of India (Annexure-D format). Persons already possessing EWS certificate in Annexure-C format also need to apply for Annexure-D format when seeking Central Govt. reservation benefits.

10. Appellate Authority: District Magistrate of the concerned district is the Appellate Authority. In Kolkata, Divisional Commissioner, Presidency Division is the Appellate Authority. Decision of the Appellate Authority shall be final.

11. Effective reservation for EWS:
I. Maintenance of 100-point roster: Gazette Notification No. 18-Emp(EC)/LABR-27011(20)/1/2020-EC dated 07.02.2023, issued by Labour Department, Government of West Bengal, is required to be followed for EWS reservation in direct recruitment.
II. Admission to Educational Institutions: As stated in OM No. 325-PAR(AR)/3P-1/2019.

12. Nodal Officer: Every Government establishment shall appoint a senior officer of the Department as the Nodal Officer to monitor the implementation of reservation for EWS Category.

List of Annexure: A – Form of Application for EWS Certificate; B – Self-Declaration; C – Statutory format of EWS certificate (applicable in this state); D – Format of EWS certificate for persons seeking EWS reservation under Government of India.

Acknowledgement Slip: Application to be heard at concerned BDO/SDO/DWO Kolkata office on 2nd or 4th Wednesday of any month within next 60 days between 12 noon and 3 pm after online submission.

Key provisions:
BCW Department acts as Nodal Department for EWS reservation
Key modification from 325-PAR: Issuing authority changed from DM/ADM/SDO to specifically Additional District Magistrate (in charge of development) and DWO Kolkata/Ex-officio Joint Director BCW & TD for Kolkata
Adds Aadhaar Card/Khadyasathi card and PAN Card as mandatory additional documents
EWS certificate validity: financial year of issuance only (annual renewal required)
Persons who shifted from other states must be WB residents to avail WB EWS reservation
OBCs in State list but not Central list: eligible for EWS under Central Govt. (Annexure-D format)
Those with Annexure-C (state) certificate must also get Annexure-D for central government purposes
Appellate Authority: District Magistrate (districts); Divisional Commissioner Presidency Division (Kolkata)
100-point EWS roster: follows Labour Department Gazette Notification No. 18-Emp(EC)/LABR-27011(20)/1/2020-EC dated 07.02.2023
Each establishment must appoint a Nodal Officer to monitor EWS reservation implementation
Hearing: 2nd or 4th Wednesday within 60 days of online submission, 12 noon to 3 pm
Circulated to: all Secretaries/Departments, all Divisional Commissioners, all District Magistrates, all PO-cum-DWO/DWOs, all SDOs, Minister PS BCW, Chief Secretary, ACS P&AR, Secretary Dept. of Social Justice & Empowerment (GoI)
